references.text: Naomi's recognition of God's goodness through her kinsman Boaz, from their first meeting (Ruth 2:20) to the fulfillment of his role as kinsman-redeemer (Ruth 4:14).
A theological parallel between the human kinsman-redeemer (go'el) in Ruth and God's own role as redeemer in Isaiah.
An identical liturgical response to God's gift of a man who secures the family line (Solomon for David, Boaz for Naomi).
Narrative inclusion: The women of the city's reaction marks the transition from Naomi's emptiness (Ruth 1:19) to her restoration (Ruth 4:14).
